title: Add two buffers, whole
starter:
%x   = buffer 4 dtype=i32 slot=0
%y   = buffer 4 dtype=i32 slot=1
%out = buffer 4 dtype=i32 slot=2
%vx  = load %x
%s   = store %out %vx
%o1  = after %out %s
hints: The starter loads only `x` and stores it unchanged. `y` is never read.
Load the whole of `y` the same way: `%vy = load %y`. That value has shape `(4,)` too.
Add the two values with `%sum = add %vx %vy`, then store `%sum` in place of `%vx`.
explain: `load` of a whole buffer gives a value of shape `(4,)`. `add` on two values of the same shape adds them element by element, and `store` of that value writes all four elements. There is no range, no counter and no view: the compiler builds the loop.
